summary: Solid infrastructure foundation. Three issues require fixes before production: (1) nginx Content-Type server-level add_header conflicts with proxied responses, (2) missing .gitignore means .env can be committed accidentally, (3) Dockerfile stage alias 'AS base' is unused (cosmetic). Several minor improvements recommended.

findings.title: Content-Type add_header at server level overwrites proxied response Content-Type
findings.description: Line 117: `add_header Content-Type 'application/json' always;` is at server level and applies to ALL responses including those proxied from memory-hub. This will incorrectly set Content-Type on MCP SSE responses (which return text/event-stream), MCP JSON-RPC responses, and the /health JSON (where upstream already sets it). The comment says it's 'for 401 JSON body' but the directive applies to every response.

findings.title: Missing .gitignore — .env can be committed accidentally
findings.description: There is no .gitignore file in the repository root. The .env.example comment says 'NEVER commit .env to git (it is in .gitignore)' but no .gitignore exists. Since MNEMONIC_IDENTITY (Ed25519 private key), MNEMONIC_JWT, and MEMORY_API_KEY are all stored in .env, an accidental `git add .` would commit them.
findings.recommendation:
Create a .gitignore at the repo root that includes at minimum:
```
.env
.env.local
*.env
!.env.example
node_modules/
```

findings.title: Dockerfile stage alias 'AS base' is unused (single-stage build)
findings.description: Line 17: `FROM oven/bun:1.3.10-slim AS base` — the `AS base` alias is only meaningful in multi-stage builds where a later stage does `COPY --from=base`. Since this is a single-stage build, the alias is vestigial and slightly misleading (implies there's a second stage that adds production artifacts on top of base).

findings.title: DATABASE_URL double-interpolation of POSTGRES_PASSWORD:?
findings.description: Line 54: `DATABASE_URL: postgres://${POSTGRES_USER:-memory}:${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:?}@postgres:5432/${POSTGRES_DB:-memory}`. The `POSTGRES_PASSWORD:?` (without error message text) will produce an unhelpful error 'required variable POSTGRES_PASSWORD is empty or unset' — compare with line 24 which has `:?POSTGRES_PASSWORD is required`. Inconsistent error messaging.
findings.recommendation:
Use consistent `:?` error messages:
```yaml
DATABASE_URL: postgres://${POSTGRES_USER:-memory}:${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:?POSTGRES_PASSWORD is required}@postgres:5432/${POSTGRES_DB:-memory}
```

findings.title: Missing client_max_body_size — memory_capture has no upload size guard at nginx
findings.description: nginx's default client_max_body_size is 1MB. The application-level limit (D8) is 10MB for memory_capture. Without setting `client_max_body_size 11m;` in the nginx config, large captures will get a 413 from nginx before reaching memory-hub. The error returned would be nginx's default HTML 413 page, not a JSON error.
findings.recommendation:
Add inside the `server` block (HTTPS section):
```nginx
client_max_body_size 11m;
```
This matches the 10MB application limit with 1MB headroom for headers and metadata.

findings.title: Bearer token comparison is case-sensitive on 'Bearer' prefix
findings.description: Line 65: `if ($http_authorization = 'Bearer $memory_api_key')` — nginx string equality is case-sensitive. An MCP client that sends `bearer <token>` (lowercase) or `BEARER <token>` will get 401 even with the correct token. RFC 7235 specifies auth-scheme tokens are case-insensitive, so 'bearer' and 'Bearer' are equivalent.
findings.recommendation: Document this in the nginx.conf comment. The simplest approach is to note the requirement for MCP clients to use `Authorization: Bearer <token>` (capital B) in the setup instructions. Alternatively use a Lua module or auth_request subrequest for case-insensitive comparison, but that adds complexity. Given this is single-user and nginx `if` has limitations, documenting the behavior is acceptable.

findings.title: Correct postgres healthcheck gates memory-hub startup
findings.description: The `depends_on: postgres: condition: service_healthy` pattern correctly prevents memory-hub from starting until Postgres is ready. Combined with the pg_isready healthcheck, this prevents gbrain's Postgres engine from attempting to connect to an uninitialized database.

findings.title: Ports correctly internal-only (expose, not ports)
findings.description: Both 3456 (memory-hub) and 5432 (postgres) use `expose:` not `ports:`. This means they are only accessible inside the Docker network. nginx is the only external entry point. This is the correct security posture for a single-user deployment.
